On Sat, Nov 28, 2026 at 09:12, Tom Barlow <tbarlow@catalogue.inc> wrote:
> Irene / Laura,
>
> Thanks for the call yesterday....

Tom / team — attached is a first-pass annotated Exhibit A (IR-annotated-Exhibit_A_redline.docx). Below are the two alternative drafting approaches we discussed:

Alternative A — 3-month rolling average true-up (concise):
"For the purposes of calculating monthly discounts under this schedule, Customer Usage shall be determined as the average of the current month and the two immediately preceding months. Such rolling-average shall be used to determine the applicable pricing band for the month. An annual true-up based on cumulative 12-month Usage shall apply to reconcile any under- or over-credits."

Notes: preserves smoothing, straightforward to explain.

Alternative B — Capped monthly excursion w/ annual true-up (slightly more conservative):
"Notwithstanding the Pricing Schedule, monthly band movement shall be limited to a maximum step of 25% (twenty-five percent) up or down relative to the prior month's applied Usage for pricing-band purposes. Any movement beyond the capped excursion shall be considered for the annual reconciliation only. Annual true-up shall reconcile to actual 12-month cumulative Usage."

Notes: Good for customers with predictability concerns but protects Redwood from short spikes. Proposed % is negotiable.

We also have a short third option (hybrid) where a 3-month rolling average applies but the monthly band movement cannot exceed 50% per month; that keeps smoothing but allows a larger catch-up.

I'll call out specific redline edits in the attached docx. Laura/Marissa — anything in the redline that is a hard NO from legal? If not, I propose we send Alternatives A and B to Catalogue with a short explanation of the revenue impact for each (one-pager).

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Commercial Strategy, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Karthik — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions before we schedule:

1) On Alternative B: the 25% cap feels tight for some of our seasonal business — if our month jumps 300% prepatory to a product launch, capping at 25% could force a very large annual true-up and distort unit economics. Would Redwood consider a two-tier cap? e.g., 25% for months < baseline and 100% for months that exceed baseline by > 150% (i.e., allow a full step-up for big launches but avoid volatility around baseline months).

2) For Alternative A: your rolling average is clean, but how would you treat partial-month onboarding (week-long pilot month) — do you treat the pilot as a full month for averaging or prorate? Our preference is to prorate initial months using actual days.

Example (from our CSV):
Account Beta — Jan: 200k tokens, Feb: 220k, Mar (launch): 900k
Using Alternative A (3-month average):
- March applied Usage = (200k + 220k + 900k)/3 = 440k
- That jumps Beta into a higher band and triggers a larger monthly credit. If you add a cap on month-over-month movement it changes the applied band.

We can live with either approach if the order form has explicit examples and an annex that shows how onboarding months and big launches are treated. Could you add those examples to the one-pager?

We can do a 30-min call Thu 12/1 11am PT. If you want to pre-send the one-pager + annotated exhibit beforehand that would speed legal review on our side.

Tom
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Tom — perfect, thanks for the specific asks. Quick responses and next steps: 

- On the two-tier cap idea: Karthik and I think that is reasonable as a negotiation path. Karthik will draft a two-tier cap illustration (25% soft cap / 100% launch carveout threshold) plus a hybrid variant that uses the 3-month rolling average but includes a launch carveout for >150% month-over-baseline. We'll include numeric examples for Beta-like scenarios.
- On pilot/proration: Redwood's standard practice is to prorate the first partial month based on actual days; we'll state that explicitly in the Annex so it is unambiguous.
- I'll have Karthik and Marissa turn the annotated Exhibit A into a one-page explainer with 2 worked examples and send that plus a proposed redline before Thu 12/1 11am PT so we can use the call to finalize.
